Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.Environment: Warm temperatures (20–30°C), high humidity, prolonged leaf wetness and frequent rainfall.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.Spread: Spread through wind-blown spores, rain splash, contaminated tools and infected plant debris.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.Description: Leaf Scorch is a common fungal disease of strawberry that reduces photosynthesis by damaging leaves. Severe infections weaken plants, reduce fruit yield and decrease fruit quality.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small purple spots appear on older leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Lesions enlarge and merge, causing reddish-brown discoloration.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Leaves become dry, scorched and die prematurely, reducing plant vigor.
Age_Cycle.Estimated: Symptoms generally develop within 7–14 days after infection under favorable conditions.

Recommended_Actions: Apply preventive fungicides during humid weather.

Strawberry___healthy.Environment: Cool to moderate temperatures (15–26°C), fertile well-drained soil (pH 5.5–6.8), adequate sunlight and consistent irrigation.
Strawberry___healthy.Description: The uploaded strawberry leaf shows no visible signs of disease, pest infestation or nutrient deficiency. The plant appears healthy and capable of producing vigorous growth and high-quality fruit.

Age_Cycle.Early: Healthy leaf emergence with bright green coloration.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Normal vegetative growth, flowering and fruit development.
Age_Cycle.Estimated: Continuous healthy growth throughout the growing season under proper crop management.

Organic_Treatment: Apply balanced organic fertilizers when needed.
Use organic mulch to conserve soil moisture.
